name: Hunter's Chicken (BBQ Bacon Cheese Bake)
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source lists 621 cal / 58g protein - the highest protein figure in the entire slice, and every ingredient is a tracked board id. Five ingredients, one baking dish, trivially scaled. NEAR-DUPE WATCH vs the live Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Chicken Bowls (same sauce, totally different build) and Slow Cooker Crack Chicken (bacon + cheese). | HARVEST: Published nutrition is for the chicken only and does not include the serving sides.
OVERRIDE Green Beans: 'veggies such as carrots, green beans or broccoli' side, no qty; house 100 g/serving
intro_html: Hunter's chicken is a British pub standard: chicken breast wrapped in bacon, painted with barbecue sauce, buried under melted cheese, and baked. Five real ingredients and one dish. It also carries the most protein of anything in this batch by a wide margin, at 668 calories and 63 grams of protein for about $2.46 a serving.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 6.25 lb: ~$20.19. Buy 7 lbs: $22.89.
BBQ Sauce, 3 cups: ~$3.67. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 18oz bottles.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.23. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $34.44 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.46 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $40.14 across 14 servings, roughly $2.87 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.28 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $46.42. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.46 a serving for the highest protein plate in the lineup. That protein per dollar is the real headline here, and it comes from a five ingredient bake anyone can make on a Tuesday.
shop_smart: Chicken breast is the biggest expense, so buy the family pack rather than the small tray. The per pound gap between the two is one of the most consistent savings in the entire store.
Barbecue sauce is worth buying by the large bottle. It costs far less per ounce than the small one, it keeps for months, and this recipe uses a real amount of it.
Buy block cheese and shred it yourself when it is cheaper than the bags, which it usually is. Bagged shreds also carry anti-caking starch that keeps them from melting as smoothly.
Frozen green beans and a bag of potatoes round out the plate for very little. Both hold up better in a container all week than most fresh vegetables would.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F. Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper and wrap each one in bacon, tucking the ends underneath so they do not unravel in the oven.

Sear the wrapped chicken in a hot dry pan for 2 minutes a side to start rendering the bacon fat. Bacon that goes straight into the oven wrapped around chicken comes out pale and flabby, and this step is the fix.
Arrange the chicken in a large baking dish and brush a generous coat of barbecue sauce over the top of each piece.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165F in the thickest part.
Scatter the shredded cheddar and mozzarella over the top and return it to the oven for 5 to 8 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges.
While the chicken bakes, cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with salt and pepper, and roast them on a separate sheet pan until crisp.
Steam or roast the green beans just until tender and still green, then let everything rest 5 minutes before packing.
portion_html: Weigh one piece of chicken into each container, then split the potatoes and green beans by weight across all fourteen. Set the dish on the scale and subtract the empty weight if you want to check yourself. Each portion lands at 668 calories, and the bacon and cheese keep the chicken from drying out on reheat, which is a real advantage over plain baked breast.

head.description: Hunter's chicken, a British bake of bacon wrapped chicken with barbecue sauce and melted cheese plus potatoes and green beans, at about $2.46 a serving.
head.keywords: hunters chicken, bbq bacon chicken bake, cheesy chicken breast, british pub food, high protein meal prep, budget chicken dinner, easy chicken bake
steps: Season the chicken breasts and wrap each in bacon.
Sear the wrapped chicken briefly on both sides to render the bacon.
Arrange in a baking dish, brush with barbecue sauce, and bake at 400F for 20 to 25 minutes.
Top with cheddar and mozzarella and bake 5 to 8 minutes more until bubbling.
Roast the potato wedges and cook the green beans, then portion everything into 14 containers.
